column7: Suspending, deactivating or deleting a user sweeps exactly two child tables (sessions via DeleteSessionsForUserExcept, personal_access_tokens via RevokeAllPersonalAccessTokensForUser) inside a transaction that row-locks the user first, but the INSERTS were not serialized against that sweep -- so a PAT minted in the window committed with revoked=false AFTER a sweep that was audited as complete. The PAT is inert while the account is blocked (ValidatePATToken re-checks account state), but ReactivateUser revokes nothing, so the routine suspend -> investigate -> reactivate sequence handed the credential back, possibly with no expiry. Fixed by inserting inside a transaction and re-reading the owner with lockLiveParent (FOR SHARE on Postgres) -- still is_active and still in a login-capable account_state -- rolling back if not. Sound because every sweep path row-locks the user BEFORE revoking, which lockLiveParent's write-then-check ordering requires. Red on real Postgres: one unrevoked PAT survived a suspend that reported success. Found by C-GUARD-3 guard 2
